definitions.explanation: The joint in the middle of the arm where it bends.

examples.japanese: {肘|ひじ}をテーブルにつかないでください。
examples.english: Please don't put your elbows on the table.

examples.japanese: {肘|ひじ}を{曲|ま}げてください。
{肘|ひじ}をぶつけてしまいました。
{子供|こども}が{肘|ひじ}をテーブルにつくのを{見|み}て、{母|はは}が「だめよ」と{言|い}いました。
examples.english: Seeing the child put their elbow on the table, the mother said "Don't do that."

examples.japanese: テニスを{長|なが}い{間|あいだ}していたので、{右|みぎ}の{肘|ひじ}が{痛|いた}くなって、{病院|びょういん}に{行|い}きました。
examples.english: Because I played tennis for a long time, my right elbow started hurting and I went to the hospital.

notes:
{肘|ひじ} is the elbow—the joint in the middle of the arm.

WRITING:
The kanji is complex, so hiragana (ひじ) is common in casual writing.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {肘|ひじ}を{曲|ま}げる: to bend one's elbow
- {肘|ひじ}をつく: to put one's elbows (on table)
- {肘|ひじ}をぶつける: to bump one's elbow
- {肘|ひじ}{掛|か}け: armrest

MANNERS:
{肘|ひじ}をつく (putting elbows on the table) is considered bad manners in Japan, as in many cultures.

RELATED BODY PARTS:
- {膝|ひざ}: knee
- {手首|てくび}: wrist
- {肩|かた}: shoulder
